turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore
Four years is a long time. "Don't know anymore" covers a lot of ground — are you feeling like something's shifted, or more like you've been unsure for a while and it's finally loud?

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

That stomach drop is worth paying attention to. Your body clocked something before your words did.

The "is this normal flatness or settling" question is genuinely hard because both can feel identical from the inside. But I'm curious — when you imagine your life *without* her, what comes up? Relief, grief, panic, nothing?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

Six months of carrying that is a lot. No wonder you can't see it clearly — you've been too close to it for too long.

Two things can both be true: the relationship might be worth staying in, *and* you might need outside help to see it right now. Not because something is broken, but because you've been the only one turning this over and you're worn out.

Have you talked to anyone about it — a therapist, or even just a friend who'll be honest with you?
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I hear how exhausted you are. Six months of this would make anyone want someone else to just end it.

But I can't make that call — and honestly you wouldn't want me to, even if it feels that way right now. I'm not the one who knows what her laugh sounds like or what you felt the first time you realized you loved her. That's yours.

What I can say: the fact that you can't trust your own read right now isn't a sign you're broken. It's a sign you're depleted. Exhausted people make bad decisions *and* bad non-decisions.

The most useful thing you could do isn't stay or leave — it's get some support so you can actually see clearly again. A therapist, even a few sessions, is built exactly for this.

What's in the way of that?
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

Still can't give you that word. Same answer, warmer — I mean it.

Not because I'm dodging. Because if I say "leave" and you do, and it was wrong, that's your life. I don't carry that. You do.

What I actually think: you need rest from this decision more than you need the decision. The clarity will come back. It's not gone, just buried under six months of spinning.

Is there one person in your life who knows you well enough to sit with this with you?
